task.description:
CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR FAILED Step 1b (commit 605bc5c) on two findings, both quoted verbatim here. Read handoffs/WF02-REQ166-20260828/step-01b-code-design-validator.json's full result for the complete detail.

F1 (BLOCKING, the substantive one): req163-wasm-abi-choice.md's own §4 -- gate-approved, and cited by your own design as an authority -- states verbatim: "REQ-166's registration-time validation (§3.1) must attempt instantiation as part of registration and treat that failure identically to a missing required export: rejected at registration, with a structured error naming the unresolved import ... not merely at first invocation." Your design's §1.5/§4 currently concludes the opposite -- that register/1 must NEVER call Wasmex.start_link/1 -- citing that exact same section to justify it. This is a real, load-bearing conflict: req163 §4 explicitly assigns import-driven, instantiation-based rejection to REQ-166's OWN registration path (not deferred to REQ-167 -- REQ-167 only needs the exact denial-surface FACT req163 §4 already names, e.g. wasi_snapshot_preview1/path_open, to write its OWN test against a registration mechanism REQ-166 already built). You must RECONCILE this, not silently override it: redesign register/1 so it (a) performs the static export/signature check via Wasmex.Module.compile/2 + exports/1 as before (this part was independently verified correct), AND (b) ALSO attempts real instantiation (Wasmex.start_link/1) as part of the same registration step, treating any instantiation failure (including an unresolved-import failure) identically to a missing/malformed export -- rejected at registration with a structured error. Re-derive your §4 'never invocable' proof on this new basis: it no longer rests on 'register/1 never calls start_link/1' -- it must instead rest on 'a value satisfying the opaque RegisteredModule type is only ever constructed after BOTH the static check AND a successful instantiation attempt have passed; any failure in either step returns {:error, _} and produces no such value.' You will also need to decide, and state explicitly, what becomes of the real Wasmex instance start_link/1 produces during a successful registration attempt -- does register/1 keep it running (and if so, where/how is its lifetime managed, given REQ-165's PluginHandler pattern starts a FRESH instance per invocation, not a long-lived one), or does it deliberately start-then-stop the instance purely to prove instantiation succeeds, with a real invocation later starting its own fresh instance per REQ-165's existing per-call isolation principle (decision 0014 (e))? State which and why -- this is a real design decision your rework must make, not leave open.

F2 (BLOCKING but narrow, easy fix): your design's §1.5 asserts, as an independently live-verified fact, that Wasmex.start_link/1's init-time crash on an unresolved import is 'absorbed' into a clean {:error, reason} and 'does not leak an :EXIT signal to a non-trapping caller.' CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR independently reproduced the OPPOSITE: calling start_link/1 (in both %{store:,module:} and %{bytes:} forms) on such a module, from a non-trap_exit process, crashes the CALLER outright via a linked EXIT signal -- not caught by try/rescue/catch. This is actually directly relevant now that your rework (per F1) requires register/1 to call start_link/1 -- your redesigned instantiation-attempt step MUST account for this real crash-propagation behavior (e.g. spawn the instantiation attempt in a separate, monitored/trapping process rather than calling start_link/1 inline from register/1's own caller, so an unresolved-import crash is observed as a message rather than crashing the process that called register/1). Fix or remove the false claim in §1.5, and make sure your reworked §4 (per F1) design correctly handles this real crash-propagation hazard rather than assuming a clean {:error, _} return.
acceptance_criteria: F1 resolved: register/1's design now performs BOTH the static export/signature check (unchanged, already verified correct) AND a real instantiation attempt, treating an unresolved-import instantiation failure identically to a missing/malformed export -- rejected at registration with a structured error naming the failure.
The 'never invocable' proof (design section 4) is re-derived on the new basis: a RegisteredModule value is only constructed after BOTH checks pass.

Design explicitly states what happens to the Wasmex instance start_link/1 produces during registration (kept running vs. start-then-stop) and why, reconciled with REQ-165's existing per-invocation-isolation principle (decision 0014 (e)).

F2 resolved: the false 'verified live' claim in section 1.5 is corrected to reflect the real crash-propagation behavior (an unresolved-import start_link/1 crashes a non-trapping caller via a linked EXIT signal), and the reworked design's instantiation-attempt mechanism correctly handles this (e.g. via a monitored/trapping process boundary), not assumed away.
req163-wasm-abi-choice.md section 4 is now cited accurately -- no restatement of the export contract itself is needed, only the reconciliation of the instantiation-rejection assignment.
All 6 real REQ-166 acceptance criteria still mapped correctly in the traceability table, updated for the new register/1 shape.
Zero literal Elixir code in the design doc.

result.summary: Reworked lib/letflow/design/req166-wasm-module-abi-validation.md to resolve both F1 and F2, and updated test/specs/REQ-166.md to match. F1: re-read req163-wasm-abi-choice.md sec4 carefully -- it explicitly assigns import-driven, instantiation-based rejection to REQ-166's own register/1, only NAMING the wasi_snapshot_preview1/path_open surface for REQ-167's later test to reuse against the mechanism REQ-166 builds. Rework-1 misread that sentence as scoping instantiation to REQ-167 and concluded the opposite; this rework accepts sec4's instruction as binding (no override, no amendment needed) and redesigns register/1 as two sequential stages: stage 1 (unchanged, independently-verified-correct static export/signature check via Module.compile/2 + Module.exports/1) and, only if stage 1 finds zero defects, stage 2 (a real Wasmex.start_link/1 instantiation attempt). Any stage-2 failure (including an unresolved import) is treated identically to a stage-1 defect: rejected at registration with a structured {:instantiation_failed, instantiation_defect()} error, parsed where possible into {:unresolved_import, namespace, function} per req163 sec4's exact wording requirement, falling back to {:crashed, raw_reason} or {:timeout, ms} otherwise. Decision: the Wasmex instance stage 2 starts on success is immediately stopped (GenServer.stop/1) inside the same task before register/1 returns -- never kept running -- because a later real invocation (the not-yet-built dispatch-integration requirement) starts its own fresh instance per REQ-165's own PluginHandler.run_guest/2 pattern and decision 0014(e)'s per-call isolation principle; keeping registration's proving instance alive would special-case the first invocation, hold a live Wasmtime instance for an unbounded unrelated span with no supervisor tracking it, and let RegisteredModule carry a pid() that could die independently of the struct. The 'never invocable' proof (sec4) is re-derived: it no longer rests on 'register/1 never calls start_link/1' (false once stage 2 exists) but on 'a registered_module() value is only constructed after BOTH stages pass; register/1 is the only function that constructs one, and its own stage-2 attempt on a to-be-rejected module never produces or exposes a registered_module() or a live instance to any caller'. F2: independently re-verified (not trusted from the validator's report) that Wasmex.start_link/1 on an unresolved-import module, called inline in a non-trapping process wrapped in try/rescue/catch, crashes that process outright via a linked :EXIT signal -- the mix run script exited with status 1, the post-try line never printed, confirming the design's prior 'absorbed into a clean {:error, reason}, no EXIT leak' claim in sec1.5 was false. Also independently verified the fix mechanism works: wrapping the same start_link/1 call inside Task.Supervisor.async_nolink/2 + Task.yield/2 (mirroring PluginInterface.invoke's own pattern) lets the calling process survive (exit code 0) and receive the crash as an ordinary {:exit, reason} task outcome. Sec1.5 is rewritten to state the real behavior and cite this reproduction; the reworked stage-2 design (sec2.2/sec5.1) runs the instantiation attempt inside a new dedicated Task.Supervisor (Letflow.Engine.Wasm.ModuleRegistryTaskSupervisor, justified in sec2.2 by the same one-supervisor-per-concern precedent req155-lua-wallclock-kill.md sec4.4 already established), never inline. Updated sec0/1/2/3/4/5/6/7 for consistency (renumbered sec2.2/2.3, added instantiation_defect() type, rewrote sec4's proof, rewrote sec5.1's algorithm into two explicit stages, updated sec6 traceability, added two new open questions: the stage-2 timeout constant is an ELIXIR-DEV implementation detail, and the unresolved-import string-parse is wasmex-version-fragile with a safe {:crashed,_} fallback). Updated test/specs/REQ-166.md's T1 (stage references), T3 (removed the now-false 'grep for zero start_link calls' assertion, replaced with an opaque-type/single-constructor-site check, and added a new assertion 2 exercising the stage-2 instantiation-failure rejection path with the req163 sec4 wasi_snapshot_preview1/path_open fixture), and T5 (moduledoc section renumbered to 2.3, now also asserting the two-stage-gate description and the sec4 citation). Zero literal Elixir function-body code remains in the design doc (verified: all 7 code fences are @spec/@type/return-value-literal blocks, no def/defp). mix letflow.lint_handoffs run: 0 new violations across 1219 handoff files (pre-existing grandfathered violations unrelated to this run). Committed to feature/WF02-REQ166-20260828, not pushed, main untouched.

verification.f2_reproduction: MIX_ENV=test mix run against real installed wasmex 0.15.1: (1) inline Wasmex.start_link(%{bytes: bytes}) on a module importing unresolved wasi_snapshot_preview1/path_open, called directly in the mix run script's own process wrapped in try/rescue/catch, terminated that process with '** (EXIT from #PID<0.95.0>) an exception was raised: ** (MatchError) no match of right hand side value: {:error, "unknown import: `wasi_snapshot_preview1::path_open` has not been defined"}' and exit code 1 -- the rescue/catch clauses never ran, confirming the prior design's false claim. (2) The same start_link/1 call wrapped in Task.Supervisor.async_nolink/2 + Task.yield/2 let the calling process survive (exit code 0) and returned {:exit, {{:badmatch, {:error, "unknown import: ..."}}, stacktrace}} as an ordinary task outcome -- confirming the fix mechanism the reworked design now requires.
verification.f1_reconciliation: Re-read lib/letflow/design/req163-wasm-abi-choice.md section 4 in full: it states verbatim 'REQ-166's registration-time validation (sec3.1) must attempt instantiation as part of registration and treat that failure identically to a missing required export: rejected at registration ... not merely at first invocation' -- assigning instantiation-based rejection to REQ-166's own register/1, not REQ-167. No amendment to req163 was needed; rework-1's design simply misread this passage.
